standard_prerequisites.name: Tableau derivability from a set
standard_prerequisites.statement: Gamma proves A in the tableau calculus when some finite {B_1,...,B_n} subset of Gamma has a closed tableau for {False A, True B_1,...,True B_n}.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the hypothesis the proof unpacks (2509-2513).

standard_prerequisites.name: Tableau soundness
standard_prerequisites.statement: The unit's soundness theorem: a closed tableau for a finite set of signed formulas cannot be satisfied, i.e., no structure satisfies all its members.
standard_prerequisites.use: It converts the closed tableau into the satisfaction disjunction (2513-2518).

core_obligations: Unpack derivability: a finite B_1,...,B_n in Gamma with a closed tableau for {False A, True B_1,...,True B_n} (2509-2513).
By tableau soundness every structure M makes some B_i false or makes A true (2513-2518).
Contrapositively, if M satisfies all of Gamma (hence all B_i), M satisfies A; so Gamma entails A (2518-2521).

proof_roadmap.step: Unpack derivability to a finite closed tableau.

difficulty_reason: The counted corollary is the author corollary at source lines 2504-2507: if Gamma proves A in the tableau calculus then Gamma entails A. The author proof (2509-2521) is complete: derivability yields a finite subset B_1,...,B_n of Gamma and a closed tableau for the signed set {False A, True B_1,...,True B_n}; the unit's tableau soundness theorem (cited by label) implies every structure either falsifies some B_i or satisfies A; hence any structure satisfying all of Gamma satisfies A. The only invoked external result is the unit's own soundness theorem, cited by label and separately proved.
